docs.title: Consumption
docs.text:
Billable API keys must be portal-linked (clients_nolain_query.user_id set). Admission reads profiles_nolain_query.credit_balance and returns HTTP 402 when the balance is empty.

Unlinked owner keys (developer keys from scripts/ensure-developer-key.sql, with tier = 'owner' and no user_id) skip credit admission and settlement. Linked owner keys follow the same rules as free/premium portal keys.

Unlinked non-owner keys are rejected with 402 (no portal account).

Charge timing: every LLM invoke inside an active billing_scope(client_id). Workers wrap stage execution; HTTP handlers wrap conversation, analyze_query, and synthesize.

Credit charges use the atomic RPCs in sql/003_account_balance.sql. Existing databases that still have query_balance should apply sql/008_credit_rename.sql. Configure Stripe packages as a JSON map, for example {"price_basic":"1000","price_team":"10000"}. The webhook accepts only paid sessions whose price_id and declared credits match this map.

docs.title: Receipts: one job, many LLM charges
docs.text:
Every time the product calls an LLM (code generation, DAG, chart, and so on), two things happen:

  1. OpenRouter runs the model. That costs us money.
  2. The app then subtracts credits from the user's account so they pay for that call.

A typical pandas job with a chart and a DAG is several LLM calls, not one. Each call should take some credits.

Two stores are involved:

  • User balance (credit_balance) — a number: how many credits the user has left.
  • Ledger (credit_balance_ledger_nolain_query) — the receipt book. Each charge adds a row: “minus 6 credits for job X”, then “minus 4 credits for the same job”, and so on.

When a charge works, both update: the balance goes down, and a new receipt is added. The receipt stores the job id so you can later ask what that query cost by summing its rows.

Receipts are tagged with event_type:

Tag Meaning llm_call One LLM call was charged. A job may have many of these. grant Credits were added (plan or Stripe top-up). settlement Reserved. At most one row of this tag per job.

The database still has a rule: at most one settlement receipt per job. That is unused today. It is kept for a future “one total row for the whole job” if we ever need it. Per-call charges use llm_call, which that rule does not cover, so a job can have many receipts.

If a later LLM call in the same job were written as settlement, the database would reject it (HTTP 409). The job would skip that stage even though the model already ran. Conversation endpoints that omit job_id never hit this rule.

Redis job billing totals are only a running scoreboard. They do not decide whether a second charge is allowed. The ledger does.

docs.title: Manual testing
docs.text:
1. Grant credits: update profiles_nolain_query set credit_balance = 1000 ...
  2. Run a pandas-only job (compile_dag: false, include_visualization: false).
  3. Poll GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{job_id} until success.
  4. Expect billing.charged_credits reflecting all LLM calls in the job.
  5. Repeat with compile_dag: true — expect higher totals (more LLM calls + tokens).
cd cloud_api && PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: Admission requires a positive credit balance for portal-linked keys. Unlinked owner developer keys skip admission and settlement. Each LLM credit charge is atomic; if writing the receipt fails, the call fails rather than continuing as if it were unpaid.

docs.title: Change checklist
docs.text:
1. Update CREDITS.md if user-visible pricing changes.
  2. Keep billing.yaml and plan grants in sync.
  3. Ensure every catalog model resolves rates (OpenRouter or yaml override).
  4. Route all LLM invokes through invoke_llm / invoke_llm_chain.

docs.title: CI/CD — how it works today
docs.text:
Three product repos + one infra repo, one VPS. Building images and deploying the stack are separate steps.

push nolain-ocr (master)                push nolain-query (main/platform)
        │                                         │
        ▼                                         ▼
  Build and push to GHCR                  Build and push to GHCR
  (OCR self-hosted runner)                (Query self-hosted runner)
        │                                         │
        ▼                                         ▼
  ghcr.io/…/nolain-ocr-{backend,frontend}   ghcr.io/…/nolain-query-{backend,website}
        │                                         │
        └─────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                          │  (manual — not automatic)
                          ▼
                Deploy platform to VPS          ← platform self-hosted runner
                          │
                          ▼
                docker compose pull && up -d    ← VPS runs pulled images

Infra setup (runners, keys, and the first-time VPS layout) belongs to the separate nolain-platform repository. This page documents the release flow after that infrastructure is available.

docs.title: 1. nolain-ocr — Build and push to GHCR
docs.text: What it does On push to master, builds backend and frontend Docker images on the VPS runner, pushes them to GHCR tagged :master, :latest, and :<git-sha>. Frontend build bakes in VITE_* values from GitHub secrets. Admin action required? One-time: GitHub secrets for every VITE_* the frontend Dockerfile expects. Per change: push to master (or Actions → Run workflow). Maintenance? Update nolain-ocr GitHub secrets when a new VITE_* build arg is added to the frontend, or when Supabase/Google/Stripe public IDs change.

docs.title: 2. nolain-query — Build and push to GHCR
docs.text: What it does On push to main / platform, builds cloud_api backend and nolainquery-website images on the Query self-hosted runner (~/actions-runner-query). Tags: :main or :platform, :latest, :<git-sha>. Website bakes in VITE_SUPABASE_* from secrets; VITE_CLOUD_API_URL=https://nolainquery.com. Admin action required? One-time: register third runner on VPS for nolain-query; set VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY secrets (same Supabase project as OCR). Per change: push branch → wait for build ✅ → run platform deploy. Maintenance? Grant nolain-platform GHCR read access to new Query packages (or extend GHCR_PAT). While testing Phase 2, platform compose uses :platform tags; switch to :main after merge.

docs.title: 3. nolain-platform — Deploy platform to VPS
docs.text: What it does On push to platform / main, or manual trigger: pulls latest platform repo on the VPS, logs into GHCR, runs docker compose pull && up -d using docker-compose.prod.yml and /opt/nolain/.env. Restarts nginx, OCR, Query, redis, celery workers. Reloads nginx config after up. Admin action required? One-time: GHCR_PAT secret on nolain-platform (read packages). Platform repo cloned on VPS with deploy key (Step 1.4 in guide). After product code changes: trigger this manually — it does not run when OCR or Query builds finish. Maintenance? Rotate GHCR_PAT before expiry. Update /opt/nolain/.env when backend runtime env vars change. Add Query keys (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, QUERY_*) once (Phase 2).

docs.title: 4. Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners (×3)
docs.text: What it does Executes workflow jobs on the VPS. One runner per repo: nolain-ocr (builds), nolain-platform (deploy), nolain-query (builds). All need the vps label. Admin action required? One-time: install and register all three; keep systemd services running (actions-runner, actions-runner-platform, actions-runner-query). Query runner may run via ./run.sh until root installs svc.sh. Maintenance? Upgrade runner version occasionally. Restart service if jobs sit in Waiting for a runner… while the runner shows Idle.

docs.title: 5. GHCR (GitHub Container Registry)
docs.text: What it does Stores built images. Platform compose references OCR :master and Query :platform (or :main after merge). Admin action required? None for day-to-day — build workflows push; deploy workflow pulls. Maintenance? Ensure nolain-platform has package read access for Query images (403 → refresh GHCR_PAT or grant package access).

docs.title: 6. VPS runtime — Docker stack + /opt/nolain/.env
docs.text: What it does Runs production containers (8 services after Phase 2). Shared Supabase keys; OCR Stripe/Mistral keys; Query DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and QUERY_* quotas. Nginx routes nolainocr.com → OCR, nolainquery.com → Query (HTTP until SSL cert; see guide Step 2.3). Admin action required? Edit .env on the VPS when backend env vars change. Point DNS nolainquery.com → VPS IP; run certbot for HTTPS. Maintenance? Backup .env and certbot/. Add Supabase redirect URL for https://nolainquery.com/**.

docs.title: 7. Domains
docs.text:
Domain Routes to nolainocr.com OCR frontend + /api → OCR backend nolainquery.com Query website + /api → Query backend

Query uses HTTP on port 80 until Let's Encrypt cert exists for nolainquery.com (DNS must point to VPS first).

docs.text: What changed What you do Backend or frontend app code 1. Push to master. 2. Wait for Build and push to GHCR ✅. 3. Deploy platform to VPS (manual). 4. Confirm nolainocr.com. New VITE_* Update OCR secrets → push → platform deploy. Backend env var Edit /opt/nolain/.env → platform deploy.

docs.text: What changed What you do Backend or website code 1. Push to platform (or main). 2. Wait for Build and push to GHCR ✅. 3. Deploy platform to VPS (manual). 4. Confirm nolainquery.com. New VITE_* Update Query repo secrets → push → platform deploy. Backend env var (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, quotas) Edit /opt/nolain/.env → platform deploy.

docs.title: Platform (nolain-platform)
docs.text:
What changed What you do Nginx / compose / infra Push to platform — deploy runs automatically.

Short version: product push → wait for build ✅ → manually run Deploy platform to VPS.

docs.title: When automation is broken
docs.text:
1. Build failed — open failed Build and push to GHCR run; fix code or restart the repo's runner service on VPS.
  2. Build OK, site still old — you likely skipped platform deploy. Run Deploy platform to VPS manually.
  3. Deploy stuck / runner idle — restart platform runner; trigger a new workflow run.
  4. Query site 301 to OCR / wrong backend — nginx config not reloaded: docker compose … exec nginx nginx -s reload or redeploy platform.
  5. Deploy fails on GHCR 403 — refresh GHCR_PAT or grant Query package access to nolain-platform.
  6. Query containers fail health — check DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in /opt/nolain/.env.

docs.text:

  • Billing service (Phase 3) not on VPS yet.

docs.title: Cloud API — Developer Setup Guide
docs.text: Everything a developer needs to do to make the Cloud API fully operational from scratch.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+
  • Docker Engine with the Docker Compose plugin
  • A Supabase project (free tier is fine)
  • An OpenRouter API key (routes all LLM calls)

docs.title: 2. Python Dependencies
docs.text:
The root setup script creates the shared .venv and installs both desktop and Cloud API dependencies:

./setup.sh

Cloud API and Celery run natively from this environment. Docker is used only for Redis.

docs.title: 3. Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a file at cloud_api/.env. Never commit this file.

# ── Supabase ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Found in: Supabase Dashboard → Project Settings → API
SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-id.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=eyJhbGciOiJI...   # "service_role" secret key (NOT the anon key)

# ── OpenRouter (LLM gateway) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your-openrouter-key-here
# OPENROUTER_API_BASE=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
# OPENROUTER_APP_URL=https://your-app.example
# OPENROUTER_APP_TITLE=Nolain Data Query

# ── LLM catalog (optional override) ─────────────────────────────────────────
# LLM_MODELS_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/custom_llm_models.yaml

# ── Stripe credit purchases (optional) ──────────────────────────────────────
# STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_...
# STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...
# STRIPE_PRICE_CREDITS_JSON={"price_basic":"1000","price_team":"10000"}

Copy from cloud_api/.env.example and fill in real values.

Policy files (defaults; some settings have env overrides — see BILLING.md):

File Purpose app/config/llm_models.yaml Model catalog, OpenRouter slugs, default model app/config/billing.yaml Credits per dollar, surplus rate, rate overrides app/config/generation.yaml Retry budgets, chain attempt ceiling, adaptive Pandas repair profiles

docs.title: Pandas repair settings
docs.text:
No setting is required for normal users. Server operators may tune:

  • cloud_api/app/config/generation.yaml
  • pandas_sandbox_max_retries: in-cloud retries for truncated, empty, or statically rejected code
  • pandas_max_retries: local-execution repair jobs
  • pandas_total_max_attempts: hard ceiling across the complete Pandas chain
  • pandas_repair_profiles: reasoning effort and max_tokens selected by failure category and retry index
  • pandas_repair_reasoning / pandas_repair_max_tokens: fallback profile
  • cloud_api/app/config/llm_models.yaml: first-pass model defaults and maximum completion tokens. Repair profiles override reasoning and token settings only on repair calls.

Restart the API and Celery workers after changing these YAML files because configuration is cached by each process.

Why the service-role key? The API reads and writes the clients_nolain_query table to validate keys. Credit balances live on profiles_nolain_query.credit_balance. The anon key cannot do this (Row-Level Security blocks it). The service-role key bypasses RLS and must stay server-side only.

docs.title: 4. Database Setup (Supabase)
docs.text:
Run the SQL migrations once in your Supabase project:

  1. Open the Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor.
  2. Fresh projects — run in order:
  3. cloud_api/sql/001_create_clients.sql
  4. cloud_api/sql/002_auth_users.sql
  5. cloud_api/sql/003_account_balance.sql
  6. Existing databases that still have a query_balance column should also run cloud_api/sql/008_credit_rename.sql.

Files 004–007 are historical upgrades superseded by 003 / 008; do not run them on a new project.

This creates the clients_nolain_query table, portal profiles, credit balances, and ledger RPCs.

docs.title: Schema overview
docs.text: Column Type Purpose id uuid Internal primary key api_key text The secret token validated on every request tier text owner / premium / free user_id uuid Portal account that owns the key (required for credits) is_active boolean false = key is suspended created_at timestamptz When the key was issued

docs.title: 5. Inserting the Owner Key
docs.text:
The owner key is inserted directly into the database (it is never hard-coded in source). It is intended as an unlinked developer credential: no user_id, no credit checks. Do not attach it to a portal profile unless you want it to spend that account's credits like any other linked key.

Generate a secure token:

python3 -c "import secrets; print('sk-owner-' + secrets.token_hex(16))"
# Example: sk-owner-3f9a1c72b4de5e01a8c9d2e3f4b5c6d7

Insert it in the Supabase SQL Editor (or adapt cloud_api/scripts/ensure-developer-key.sql):

insert into public.clients_nolain_query (api_key, tier, label, is_active)
values (
    'sk-owner-3f9a1c72b4de5e01a8c9d2e3f4b5c6d7',
    'owner',
    'Developer (unrestricted)',
    true
);

Save this key somewhere safe (e.g. a password manager). It is your root credential.

docs.title: 6. Inserting Client Keys (Portal / Manual)
docs.text:
The Nolain portal website will do this automatically when a user registers and requests a key. For now, insert keys manually:

# Generate a free-tier key
python3 -c "import secrets; print('sk-free-' + secrets.token_hex(8))"

-- Insert a free-tier client
insert into public.clients_nolain_query (api_key, tier)
values ('sk-free-abcdef1234567890', 'free');

-- Insert a premium-tier client
insert into public.clients_nolain_query (api_key, tier)
values ('sk-premium-1234567890abcdef', 'premium');

-- Deactivate a key
update public.clients_nolain_query set is_active = false where api_key = 'sk-free-abcdef1234567890';

docs.title: 7. Starting the Services
docs.text:
The Cloud API now uses an asynchronous architecture with Celery and Redis.

From the repository root, start all cloud development services in one terminal:

./scripts/launch-cloud-dev.sh

The launcher:

  • starts only Redis from cloud_api/docker-compose.dev.yml;
  • waits for Redis before starting the native processes;
  • runs Uvicorn and Celery from the root .venv;
  • waits for both services to become ready; and
  • stops Uvicorn, Celery, and its Redis container on exit.

Start the desktop stack in a second terminal:

./launch.sh

Press Ctrl+C in each terminal to stop that launcher's services. The Cloud API health endpoint is http://127.0.0.1:8000/health; the local execution engine is http://127.0.0.1:8001/health.

For production: - Use gunicorn with Uvicorn workers for the API. - Use a process manager like supervisord or systemd to keep the Celery worker alive.

docs.title: API key auth (desktop app / Cloud API)
docs.text:
• app/core/db.py — Supabase client singleton (reads SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY).
  • app/core/security.py — get_api_key() FastAPI dependency; validates key and enforces remaining credits.
  • app/routers/generation.py — Injects ClientContext via Depends(get_api_key).

docs.title: Credit enforcement logic
docs.text:
1. Look up api_key in clients_nolain_query.
  2. Unlinked owner keys (tier = 'owner', no user_id) skip credit checks and charges.
  3. Portal-linked keys (any tier, including owner with user_id): read profiles_nolain_query.credit_balance; return HTTP 402 when balance is empty.
  4. Unlinked non-owner keys: return HTTP 402 (not linked to a portal account).
  5. Otherwise proceed. Each LLM call charges credits immediately from token usage plus surplus (app/core/llm_billing.py, app/core/credit_pricing.py).

docs.title: LLM routing
docs.text:
• app/core/llm_config.py — OpenRouter client factory and model catalog (llm_models.yaml).
  • app/routers/llm.py — GET /api/v1/llm/models for client model selection.
  • Requests pass an optional model field (catalog id, e.g. deepseek-v4-flash-0731); omit it to use the server default.

docs.title: Stripe top-ups (optional)
docs.text:
• app/routers/billing.py — POST /api/billing/stripe/checkout and webhook handler.
  • Requires STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and STRIPE_PRICE_CREDITS_JSON.

docs.title: Portal auth (Google + Supabase, /api/auth/*)
docs.text:
See AUTH_SETUP.md for Google Cloud and Supabase dashboard configuration.

  • app/core/user_auth.py — Validates Supabase Bearer tokens via get_current_user.
  • app/routers/auth.py — Account profile and API-key CRUD for signed-in users.
  • sql/002_auth_users.sql — Profiles table and clients_nolain_query.user_id linkage.

docs.title: 9. Rotating the Owner Key
docs.text:
1. Generate a new key (step 5 above).
  2. Insert the new key into clients_nolain_query with tier = 'owner'.
  3. Set is_active = false on the old key (or delete it).
  4. Update your password manager / secrets store.

No server restart required — the change takes effect on the next request.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text:
This document is the catalog of observability the product actually emits: job progress, per-attempt generation diagnostics, token and latency totals, credit receipts, conversation session state, health pings, and structured logs.

There is no OpenTelemetry SDK, Langfuse, Prometheus, Flower, Sentry, or third-party APM. Celery task_send_sent_event / Flower event streaming is not enabled. What exists is first-party state in Redis, a credit ledger in Supabase, Celery’s result backend, and Python logs.

Related docs: SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md (pipeline), CONVERSATION_WORKFLOW.md (chat loop), BILLING.md (credits), CLOUD_API_USAGE.md (status payload).

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
Process How it runs (dev) What it emits Cloud API (FastAPI / Uvicorn, port 8000) scripts/launch-cloud-dev.sh HTTP health, conversation session Redis, classifier logs, per-call credit charges without a job id, status polling surface Celery worker (data_query_tasks) same launcher: celery -A app.core.celery_app worker --loglevel=info Redis job_state:{job_id}, Celery result backend, structured attempt logs, per-call credit charges with a job id Redis Docker from the launcher Job state (1 h TTL), conversation sessions (24 h TTL), Celery broker + result backend Supabase hosted Credit balance + credit_balance_ledger_nolain_query receipts Local Python engine (port 8001) launch.sh Execution results posted back to the Cloud API; no generation telemetry of its own Desktop (Tauri) launch.sh Polls job status; posts /conversation/result; does not persist worker diagnostics locally

OpenRouter is the LLM gateway. Token counts and finish_reason come from LangChain AIMessage.usage_metadata / response_metadata after each invoke. The app does not scrape OpenRouter’s dashboard.

docs.title: Stores
docs.text:
Celery worker / Cloud API
  ├─ Redis  job_state:{job_id}          1 hour   running scoreboard for one generation job
  ├─ Redis  conversation:{session_id} 24 hours  chat thread, last job, exec-repair history
  ├─ Redis  celery-as-broker/backend    Celery task metadata (execution_status)
  ├─ Redis  job_charge:{job_id}        unused today (legacy settlement lock)
  ├─ stdout logs                       pandas_generation_attempt, pandas_attempt_outcome, …
  └─ Supabase ledger                   durable credit receipts (event_type=llm_call)

GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id} is the read API for job telemetry. Redis is authoritative; Celery AsyncResult is a fallback when Redis has no row (unusual for current jobs).

docs.title: Celery worker
docs.text:
The worker is the main telemetry producer. Admission queues code_generator_task with a stable task_id that is the job_id. That task builds a Plan and dispatches run_stage_task once per Stage (and again on sandbox retry). Legacy v1 still uses planner_task → compiler_task → routing_task.

Worker settings that affect observability (app/core/celery_app.py):

Setting Value Effect task_track_started true GET /get_task_status can show Celery STARTED, not only PENDING / SUCCESS / FAILURE task_acks_late true A killed worker redelivers the task; job_state may already contain partial token/billing totals worker_prefetch_multiplier 1 One job at a time per worker process

The status poll payload includes both:

  • execution_status — Celery (PENDING, STARTED, SUCCESS, FAILURE, …)
  • dag_status — product pipeline status from Redis (generating_code, success, …)

docs.title: Job lifecycle (job_state:{job_id})
docs.text:
Created by queue_generation_task before apply_async. Ownership (client_id) is set once and cannot be overwritten by later worker updates. Cancellation wins over late status writes.

Initial fields:

Field Meaning status queued client_id API-key client that owns the job cancel_requested / cancel_requested_at / cancelled_at / cancelled_by Cooperative cancel created_at UTC ISO timestamp billing.model_id Catalog model id from the request (scoreboard seed; totals accumulate later)

Every Stage then merges through update_job_state (app/core/job_state.py). Token maps are additive. Result maps overwrite keys except the protected ownership/cancel fields.

docs.title: Pipeline status values
docs.text:
Pandas Plan (app/generation/plans/artifact_graph.py):

Stage status while running status when the stage succeeds (queued, plan persisted) queued — generate_pandas generating_code code_generated compile_dag compiling_from_code compiled format_visualization formatting_visualization visualization_formatted validate_visualization validating_visualization visualization_validated validate_dag validating validated finalize_plan finalizing success (written by finalize_success)

Cross-cutting statuses: retrying (sandbox or compiler retry queued), failed, cancelled. Optional-stage failure does not fail the job: the worker records the slot as failed and continues.

Legacy v1 (planner_task chain): planning, planning_completed, compiling, compiled, validating, retrying, success, failed.

docs.title: Plan and artifact scoreboard
docs.text:
Persisted on every _persist_plan_fields write:

Field Meaning capability_id Always data_analysis today plan_id data_analysis/pandas plan Full Plan dict (stage ids, options, status labels) current_stage / stage_index Stage currently running or just finished compile_dag / include_visualization Request options that shaped the Plan artifacts[] Typed envelope written at success (kind, schema_version, storage_key, payload) artifact_slots[] Canvas slots: { kind, status, reason? } requested_artifact_kinds Kinds the request asked for

Slot status values (build_artifact_slots): not_requested, pending, ready, failed, skipped.

docs.title: Retry and attempt counters
docs.text:
Field Meaning pandas_retries Sandbox retries used in this job (sandbox_max - pandas_sandbox_retries_left at accept/reject time) pandas_sandbox_retries_left Remaining in-cloud generate_pandas retries (reset on each runtime-repair job) pandas_retries_left Remaining local-exec repair jobs (POST /conversation/result) pandas_attempts_used LLM generate/repair calls consumed across the whole chain (sandbox + runtime repair jobs) pandas_total_max_attempts Hard ceiling (generation.yaml, default 9) generation_attempts Bounded list of per-call diagnostics (see below) last_pandas_error Last sandbox/preflight/runtime error string last_failed_code Last rejected pandas candidate (not executable) compiler_retries Compiler/viz retries used (max_retries - retries_left) last_compiler_error Last DAG compile/validate error errors[] Current failure list (cleared on success) pandas_code / graph / visualization_spec Latest accepted artifacts. Rejected pandas candidates are stored as last_failed_code, not as executable pandas_code.

Runtime repair copies pandas_attempts_used, generation_attempts, and error history from the previous job into the new job’s worker config so the chain ceiling is not reset. It resets pandas_sandbox_retries_left to pandas_sandbox_max_retries so a depleted sandbox budget cannot block in-job retries on the repair.

docs.title: Token and latency totals
docs.text:
Every Stage that returns StageResult.tokens feeds update_job_state(..., tokens=...). The merge is cumulative for the job:

Field Source Notes input_tokens tokens.input_tokens or prompt_tokens Sum across all billed LLM calls in this job output_tokens tokens.output_tokens or completion_tokens Visible completion tokens as reported by the provider reasoning_tokens output_token_details.reasoning Sum; 0 when the model does not report hidden reasoning llm_times[] tokens.llm_time when > 0 Per-call wall time in seconds (pandas generate currently sets this) total_llm_time sum of those Same unit

Compiler, visualization formatter, planner, and semantic-agent-on-worker paths pass LangChain usage_metadata through as tokens. They usually do not set llm_time, so llm_times is pandas-generation-centric.

HTTP-side LLM calls (intent classifier, semantic analysis, answer synthesizer) are billed but do not land in this job_state. Poll get_task_status for worker usage only. Conversation classifier/semantic charges appear only on the Supabase ledger (no job_id).

docs.title: Per-attempt diagnostics (generation_attempts)
docs.text:
This is the structured contract between CodeGeneratorService.generate and the rest of the stack. One object per pandas LLM call, kept to the last pandas_total_max_attempts entries.

Emitted twice as JSON logs, then stored on the job:

  1. pandas_generation_attempt — immediately after the LLM returns, before preflight (code_generator.py).
  2. pandas_attempt_outcome — after accept/reject, with outcome fields (data_analysis.py).

docs.title: Fields written at invoke time
docs.text: Field Meaning attempt_index 0-based index in the chain (pandas_attempts_used before this call) retry_source initial (first pass), sandbox (in-job preflight retry), runtime (local exec repair job) trigger_category Failure category that caused this call (none on first pass) policy_profile catalog on first pass; otherwise a pandas_repair_profiles key (syntax, length, runtime, repeated_failure, …) reasoning_effort Effective reasoning effort (none / low / medium / …) max_tokens Completion cap used for this call finish_reason Provider finish reason (stop, length, …) from response_metadata input_tokens This call only output_tokens This call only reasoning_tokens Hidden reasoning tokens for this call latency_seconds Wall time around the invoke code_length Characters of extracted code (0 if empty)

docs.title: Fields added after preflight
docs.text:
Field Meaning outcome accepted or rejected failure_category null when accepted; otherwise length, empty_output, syntax, invalid_unicode, sandbox_policy, runtime, … error_summary First error string, truncated to 300 characters (rejected only) error_signature Stable {category}:{normalized message} for repeated-failure detection

Categories are defined in app/generation/llm_call_policy.py. repeated_failure is a policy profile, not an outcome category: if the same signature appears twice in history, the next repair uses the repeated_failure profile.

A truncated completion (finish_reason=length) records failure_category=length on the attempt, but the history entry keeps the previous actionable error and sets truncated=true. The next repair prompt still targets that error; call parameters may use the length profile (no reasoning, higher max_tokens) so hidden reasoning cannot replace the original defect as the repair target.

Sandbox rejects that still have budget set job status to retrying and re-queue run_stage_task for generate_pandas. Exhaustion sets failed and zeroes pandas_sandbox_retries_left.

docs.title: Job billing scoreboard
docs.text:
While a stage runs, run_stage_task wraps the Stage in billing_scope(client_id, job_id=job_id). Every invoke_llm / invoke_llm_chain then:

  1. Charges the portal balance (llm_call ledger row with this job_id).
  2. Increments Redis billing on the same job.
billing field Meaning model_id Seeded at queue time (request model) token_credits Sum of token-derived credits surplus_credits Sum of surplus charged_credits token_credits + surplus_credits llm_calls Number of billed invokes in this job surplus_rate Rate from the first charge

This is a running scoreboard, not the source of truth for “may we charge again.” The ledger is. Failed and cancelled jobs keep charges for calls that already completed. Unlinked owner developer keys skip settlement; Redis totals may still increment if a charge dict is produced, but charge_client_balance_sync returns success without writing a receipt.

job_charge:{job_id} helpers in job_state.py are unused. They are leftover from a single-settlement design.

docs.title: Celery result backend
docs.text:
Each task return value is stored in Redis as the Celery result. Typical payloads:

  • code_generator_task: { job_id, capability_id, plan_id, stages }
  • run_stage_task: { status, next_stage, artifacts } or { status: retrying, … } or terminal { status, pandas_code, graph, … }

The poll endpoint prefers Redis dag_status and artifacts. execution_status is the only Celery-native field routinely shown to clients.

_celery_retries (self.request.retries) is passed into finalize_success as celery_retries. Finalize no longer retries charging; the argument is unused.

docs.title: Structured logs (worker stdout)
docs.text:
Dev workers run at --loglevel=info. Useful lines:

Logger / prefix When pandas_generation_attempt {json} After every pandas LLM call pandas_attempt_outcome {json} After accept or reject (includes outcome) Pandas code generation returned empty content (finish_reason=…, reasoning_preview=…) Empty extract; warning Error updating job status: … Redis write failed inside _update_job_status (printed, not logged)

Grep worker logs for pandas_generation_attempt or pandas_attempt_outcome to reconstruct a job without polling.

docs.title: Cloud API process
docs.text: The API process does not run Stages. It admits work, charges HTTP-side LLM calls, and exposes telemetry.

docs.title: Health (GET /health)
docs.text:
runtime_health() pings Redis and celery inspect ping (1 s timeout), then adds Supabase config:

{
  "status": "ok" | "degraded",
  "services": {
    "redis": { "ok": true },
    "celery": { "ok": true, "workers": ["celery@host"] },
    "supabase": { "ok": true, "host": "….supabase.co" }
  }
}

Generation endpoints return 503 when Redis or a worker is down (ensure_generation_runtime). This is liveness, not per-job telemetry.

docs.title: Intent classification
docs.text:
IntentClassifierService logs:

Intent classified: {intent} (confidence=…, capability=…, plan=…)

Conversation may also log Escalating meta_question to data_query (requires file computation).

These calls run inside billing_scope(client_id) without job_id. Credits hit the ledger; they never appear on get_task_status.

docs.title: Semantic analysis
docs.text: POST /api/v1/analyze_query (and the conversation graph’s analysis node) accumulate n_in_tokens_semantic / n_out_tokens_semantic on the agent instance. The analyze endpoint returns them on the SemanticAnalysis object. Conversation does not copy those counters onto the session.

docs.title: Answer synthesis
docs.text: POST /api/v1/conversation/synthesize bills inside billing_scope(client_id) with no job id. Failures log Answer synthesis failed.

docs.title: Conversation session (conversation:{session_id})
docs.text:
TTL 24 hours. Not a substitute for job_state; it is the chat control plane.

Field Role in telemetry / repair session_id / client_id Ownership messages[] { role, content, intent, timestamp } plus exec_error on execution_result rows query_state Structured follow-up state current_dag / current_result Last local execution (result, exec_error) last_task_id Job to poll; also the job whose retry budgets are copied on repair last_generation_* Query, metadata, model, Plan options for repair without re-classifying pandas_error_history Cross-job error entries (errors, code, category, error_signature)

GET /api/v1/conversation/{session_id} returns this document (minus internals the schema omits).

docs.title: Status poll (GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id})
docs.text: Auth-only (readable after credits hit zero). Maps Redis job_state to the client payload: pipeline status, artifacts, retry counters, generation_attempts, usage totals, billing, plan/slot fields. See CLOUD_API_USAGE.md for a full example.

docs.title: Local engine and desktop
docs.text:
The sidecar executes Artifacts. It does not call LLMs and does not write job_state.

After POST /execute_pandas (and optional DAG execute), the desktop posts:

POST /api/v1/conversation/result
{ session_id, pandas_code?, exec_error?, exec_result?, dag? }

That is the only execution telemetry the control plane receives. On exec_error with remaining pandas_retries_left and chain attempts left, the API queues a new generation job (status: repairing) and copies attempt history forward with retry_source=runtime.

The sidecar logs load/runtime errors to its own logger (safe_pandas_executor). Those lines never reach Cloud API logs unless the desktop forwards exec_error.

docs.title: Supabase credit ledger
docs.text:
Durable billing telemetry. Table credit_balance_ledger_nolain_query (sql/003_account_balance.sql):

Column Meaning user_id Portal user delta Negative for charges reason llm_call for model invokes job_id Set for worker calls; null for classifier / semantic / synthesize event_type llm_call, grant, settlement (unused), adjustment metadata Credit math for that call (model_id, model_cost_usd, token_credits, surplus_*, charged_credits) created_at When the receipt was written

Sum delta where job_id = … to reconstruct worker cost. HTTP-side calls have no job id, so they cannot be joined to a generation job except by time and user.

docs.title: What is not collected
docs.text: Absent Consequence Trace / span IDs Cannot stitch classifier → worker → sidecar in one trace Per-stage latency except pandas llm_time Compiler/viz duration is not in llm_times Prompt / completion text in job_state Only code_length, error_summary, and artifacts Model name per attempt Scoreboard has request model_id; attempts do not repeat it Sidecar CPU, row counts, exec wall time Only exec_error / exec_result preview Celery Flower / task events No event monitor Prometheus / OTLP No metrics scrape endpoint job_charge:* Helpers exist; nothing calls them

docs.title: How to read a job
docs.text:
1. Live: GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id} until dag_status is success, failed, or cancelled. Inspect generation_attempts, billing, token totals, and artifact_slots.
  2. Worker logs: grep pandas_generation_attempt and pandas_attempt_outcome (JSON after the prefix).
  3. Redis: GET job_state:{job_id} (TTL 1 hour). Conversation repair context: GET conversation:{session_id}.
  4. Money: ledger rows with that job_id. Conversation overhead is ledger rows with job_id null around the same time.
  5. Health: GET /health if jobs never leave queued.

docs.text: Concern Code Celery app / worker flags cloud_api/app/core/celery_app.py Queue + health cloud_api/app/core/runtime.py Redis job merge / TTL / cancel cloud_api/app/core/job_state.py Plan stage tasks cloud_api/app/tasks/pandas_generation.py Legacy v1 tasks cloud_api/app/tasks/generation.py Status poll cloud_api/app/routers/generation.py Attempt object + logs cloud_api/app/services/code_generator.py Outcome / retry / chain ceiling cloud_api/app/generation/capabilities/data_analysis.py Failure categories / repair profiles cloud_api/app/generation/llm_call_policy.py, cloud_api/app/config/generation.yaml Token charge + job billing cloud_api/app/core/llm_billing.py, cloud_api/app/core/llm_config.py Ledger cloud_api/app/core/account_balance.py, cloud_api/sql/003_account_balance.sql Conversation session + runtime repair cloud_api/app/services/conversation_manager.py Artifact slot derivation cloud_api/app/generation/plans/artifact_graph.py

docs.title: Query costs and benchmark results
docs.text:
This page reports observed execution costs instead of modeled case tables. Each run contains 50 hard retail-invoice questions using the desktop conversation loop, a local Pandas engine, and the dataset recorded in each run's parameters.txt.

Credits are the product's charged credits, not US dollars. The current default is 1,000 credits per dollar plus a 100% surplus; see CREDITS.md for the user-facing formula.

docs.title: GPT-5.6 Luna, Pandas only
docs.text:
Run: 2026-08-31_08-48-40

  • 50 queries; 49 code executions succeeded (98%).
  • 204 credits were charged: 4.08 average, 4 median, and 8 maximum per query.
  • No Pandas, sandbox, runtime, or compiler retries occurred.
  • Ground-truth comparison was unavailable.

docs.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, Pandas only
docs.text:
Run: 2026-08-31_09-15-16

  • 50 queries; 35 code executions succeeded (70%).
  • 138 credits were charged: 2.76 average, 2 median, and 8 maximum per query.
  • 23 Pandas retries occurred: 21 sandbox retries and 2 runtime repairs.
  • Ground-truth comparison was unavailable.

docs.title: GPT-5.6 Luna, Pandas plus DAG
docs.text:
Run: 2026-08-31_09-42-01

  • 50 queries; all 50 code executions succeeded (100%).
  • 45 DAG executions succeeded (90%).
  • 1,942 credits were charged: 38.84 average, 42 median, and 50 maximum per query.
  • 1 Pandas retry and 1 sandbox retry occurred; no runtime retries occurred.
  • Pandas and DAG outputs matched for 12 of 38 comparable queries (31.58%).
  • 87 compiler retries occurred, averaging 1.74 per query.
  • Ground-truth comparison was unavailable.

docs.title: What these runs show
docs.text:
• Adding DAG compilation greatly increased observed cost in this sample: 38.84 average credits versus 4.08 for GPT-5.6 Luna without a DAG.
  • The successful code rate was higher with the DAG run, but DAG execution was not perfect and its output matched Pandas in only 31.58% of comparable cases.
  • The DeepSeek run was cheaper, but its 70% code success rate and 23 retries show that cost alone does not describe the user experience.

These are measurements from one 50-query slice, not a price guarantee or a quality benchmark for every dataset. None of the three runs had ground-truth answers, so accuracy against a known correct answer cannot be concluded.

docs.title: How to reproduce
docs.text:
The benchmark instructions and output-file definitions are in benchmarks/custom_2/README.md. The raw statistics are available in each linked run directory:

  • 09-42-01 stats
  • 09-15-16 stats
  • 08-48-40 stats

Worker token totals and per-call billing fields are exposed in the benchmark JSON output. Conversation classifier, semantic-analysis, and optional answer framing calls are not included in these run totals.
